newsitem.title: UK: No OPEC plan to raise output ceiling - Gulf source.
newsitem.headline: No OPEC plan to raise output ceiling - Gulf source.

text.p: OPEC, including linchpin Saudi Arabia, has no plans to increase crude output quotas when the oil producer group next meets in November, a Gulf source said on Thursday.
OPEC's best option was to extend the current 25.033 million barrel per day (bpd) collective output ceiling for the group's 11 members, the Gulf source said.
"As things stand right now there is no plan to increase the ceiling for the next meeting," the Gulf source said. "The most likely option is an extension of the current ceiling."
The Gulf source said there were too many unknown factors in the market for OPEC to risk raising its ceiling at the November 27 meeting in Vienna despite crude prices now running at five year highs.
He said the possibilities of a mild northern hemisphere winter and an unexpectedly early return of Iraqi crude under the postponed U.N. oil-for-food exchange deal both held a risk for oil markets.
"There is still uncertainty about the weather and its impact on supply and demand this winter," the source said. "And there is still uncertainty about Iraq and when they will return to the market."
Limited Iraqi oil sales, expected under a U.N. agreement reached in May, were put on hold after Baghdad sent troops into its semi-autonomous northern Kurdish territories last month.
Most analysts do not expect Iraqi oil to start flowing until the beginning of next year at the earliest.
The Gulf source said there was also a reluctance in OPEC to open up a debate on how to divide any ceiling increase at a time when high oil prices were swelling member country coffers.
"We don't want to get into redistributing quotas at this point," the Gulf source said. "Nobody wants to rock the boat."
Most OPEC members, with the exception of Saudi Arabia and its Gulf neighbours the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Kuwait, are already ignoring official quotas and pumping at capacity.
A Reuter survey of OPEC production in September found output running at 25.86 million bpd compared to the 25.033 million ceiling.
When OPEC last met in June it raised its ceiling to allow for an estimated additional 800,000 bpd of Iraqi exports, yet to be realised, under the U.N. oil-for-food plan.
Other than Iraq, OPEC members have kept the same quotas since November 1993.

World oil prices hit new post-Gulf War highs this week with benchmark Brent Blend crude futures touching a high of $24.70 a barrel as buyers in Europe and the United States scrambled to replenish depleted heating oil inventories.
OPEC as a result is expected to enjoy at least an extra $25 billion of oil export revenues this year, analysts estimate.
